html:
A Chinese official, general and thinker of the Ming dynasty, after Zhu Xi the most important figure of Neo-Confucianism.

Zhu Xi had taught that one finds the right way by studying things in the outside world and the classics. Wang tried this as a young man by staring at bamboo for days to grasp its principle, and only made himself ill. Exiled to a poor post in Guizhou after offending a powerful eunuch, he had a sudden insight: the principle is already in one's own mind. Everyone has an inborn knowledge of good.

From this came his best known teaching, the unity of knowing and acting. To truly know that something is right is already to do it; knowing without doing is not knowing. He also proved an able general, putting down a prince's revolt in 1519.

His school spread widely in late Ming China. In Japan, as Yōmeigaku, it inspired activist samurai, and several leaders of the Meiji Restoration drew on it.
sum: A Chinese official, general and thinker of the Ming dynasty, after Zhu Xi the most important figure of Neo-Confucianism.
